questions.question: What is a protostar?
choices: A contracting concentration of gas and dust forming a star
A cooled planet orbiting two stars
A fully formed white dwarf
An isolated comet nucleus

questions.question: What process powers a star during its main-sequence stage?
choices: Chemical combustion of hydrogen with oxygen
Fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core
Nuclear fission of uranium
Gravitational heating as the only continuing source

questions.question: What primarily determines a star's main-sequence lifetime and later evolution?
choices: Its distance from Earth
Its apparent position in a constellation
Its initial mass
The number of planets seen nearby

questions.question: Which star color generally indicates the highest surface temperature?
choices: Red
Orange
Yellow
Blue

questions.question: What is luminosity?
choices: A star's total energy output per unit time
Its brightness only as seen from Earth
Its distance from a telescope
The mass of its planets

questions.question: What is a white dwarf?
choices: A cool giant powered by hydrogen fusion in its core
A dense stellar remnant that gradually cools
A gas cloud before a star begins forming
A massive star before its core collapses

questions.question: What is a core-collapse supernova?
choices: The ordinary daily rotation of a star
A planet reflecting sunlight
An explosion associated with collapse of a massive star's core
The slow cooling of every white dwarf

questions.question: Why does a forming protostar heat as it contracts?
choices: The gas cools because compression always removes internal energy
Its light comes only from nearby stars and no internal heating occurs
Contracting gas loses energy without any rise in temperature
Gravitational energy is converted into thermal energy

questions.question: What supports a main-sequence star against gravitational collapse?
choices: Outward pressure associated with its hot interior
A solid outer shell holds the hot gas in place
Nearby planets pull the star outward strongly enough to support it
Rotation alone supplies all support in every star

questions.question: Why do very massive stars generally have shorter main-sequence lifetimes than lower-mass stars?
choices: They use fuel more slowly despite their higher luminosity
They use their nuclear fuel at much higher rates
They contain no usable hydrogen at birth
They exhaust fuel because distance from Earth is greater

questions.question: Why may two equally luminous stars appear different in brightness?
choices: Luminosity is identical to apparent brightness
The farther one must have less mass
They may be at different distances
Both must have different surface temperatures

questions.question: What happens when a Sun-like star leaves the main sequence?
choices: It immediately becomes a black hole regardless of its mass
It remains exactly unchanged because hydrogen depletion has no effect
It turns all of its material into a planet
It expands toward a red-giant stage after core hydrogen is depleted

questions.question: What is a planetary nebula in stellar evolution?
choices: Gas shed by a dying lower-mass star surrounding its remnant
A cloud made only by colliding planets
A new solar system made entirely of planets
The solid surface of a white dwarf

questions.question: Why can supernovae contribute to the chemical enrichment of later star systems?
choices: They remove every heavy element from space
They eject material containing elements made in stars and explosions
They turn every element into hydrogen only
They prevent future clouds from forming

questions.question: How is a neutron star different from an ordinary main-sequence star?
choices: It continues ordinary hydrogen fusion in a large gas envelope
It is less dense than an ordinary main-sequence star
It is a compact remnant rather than a hydrogen-fusing star
It is an expanding shell of gas with no central remnant

questions.question: A blue star and a red star have similar observed sizes. Which generally has the hotter surface?
choices: The red star
Both must have exactly equal temperatures
Color gives no information about temperature
The blue star

questions.question: A star loses its outer gas layers and leaves a white dwarf. Which type of progenitor is most consistent?
choices: A star with initial mass similar to the Sun
Any star regardless of initial mass
A rocky planet with no fusion history
A cold interstellar grain

questions.question: Two stars have equal luminosity, but one is twice as far away. Ignoring dust, how bright does it appear relative to the nearer one?
choices: Half as bright
One-fourth as bright
Equally bright
Four times as bright

questions.question: A massive stellar core collapses and leaves a very dense compact object. Which pair lists possible remnants?
choices: A white dwarf or a normal hydrogen-burning star
A red giant or a protostar
A neutron star or a black hole
A planetary nebula or a new molecular cloud

questions.question: Why is a star cluster useful for comparing stellar life cycles?
choices: Every cluster star begins with the same mass
Cluster stars never leave the main sequence
All cluster stars must have identical luminosity
Its stars often formed at roughly the same time but have different masses
